opener_episode.title: The #1 Investing Habit That Made Me a Billionaire | David Adelman
opener_episode.why: Most recent guest episode squarely about how the very wealthy invest, which sets up Avery's insider view of how celebrities and HNW buyers approach art as an asset. Its 'insider reveals X' title pattern is the one BigDeal uses for expert guests. Alternative if a fresher hook is wanted: Joe Hudson (2026-09-21) on how billionaire CEOs make decisions.

angles.headline: How the art market really makes money (from the dealer's side)
angles.pitch: Avery, who advises celebrities, athletes and HNW buyers, explains how blue-chip art is priced and sold and what that means for anyone tempted to treat art as an investment.
angles.builds_on: David Adelman investing episode (2026-08-24); Codie's wealth and money-habit themes

angles.headline: The contrarian bet: an online-only blue-chip gallery in 2015
angles.pitch: When collectors were expected to see work in person, Avery launched ArtLife.com online-only, scaled it into an eight-figure-a-year business and coined 'Click & Mortar', a model since widely copied.
angles.builds_on: Codie's 'contrarian thinking' brand; 'How to Build a Business That Makes Money Without You' (2026-08-17)

angles.headline: Negotiating with the famous: fame, money and outlandish requests
angles.pitch: Stories from placing art with clients like Kris Jenner (a $100K+ Hap Tivey work at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024) and Scott Disick, and what they teach about asking for, and getting, top price.
angles.builds_on: 'How To Ask For More Money (And Actually Get It)' (2026-09-10); Kwame Christian negotiation episode
